title: Chiapas-Style Ground Beef, Cabbage, and White Beans

source.text: Steve Sando with Julia Newberry, The Bean Book (Rancho Gordo), p. 241, after Diana Kennedy

beans: white, cooked (any bean that holds its shape)

steps.text: Saute mode only, no pressure cook. Works the same in a large heavy skillet over medium heat.

steps.action: Mix, rest a few min to season:
Saute, medium, until onion is translucent (~1 min):
items: ¼ cup white onion, finely chopped

steps.action: Add in, cook until most juice is absorbed (~3 min):
items: 1 medium tomato (6 oz), finely chopped (or ½ cup canned diced)

steps.action: Add in, stir occasionally until browned (~7 min):
Add in, stir occasionally until moist but not juicy (~15 min):
items: 1½ cups cooked white beans, drained (e.g. Rancho Gordo Ayocote Blanco)
½ cup fresh cilantro, roughly chopped, firmly packed
Or use as a stuffing for chiles

edits: Already single-pot as written: all Saute, no pressure step, since the beans go in cooked and pressure would overcook the cabbage. 1½ cups cooked is about ½ cup dry (~¼ lb); cook those first per Fundamentals
Source gives no salt amount for the garlic paste; left as salt to taste
~1 min for translucent onion is the source's time; expect 2 to 3 min in practice
Source note: black beans with green cabbage look muddy; purple cabbage works with any bean
